name: @voxgig/sdkgen-langpack
description: Additional language targets for the Voxgig SDK Generator: Dart, Haskell and Lean.
author: Richard Rodger (http://richardrodger.com)
_peer_comment: A PACKAGED TARGET INHERITS SDKGEN'S PEERS AS ITS OWN. All three targets'
components import @voxgig/sdkgen, @voxgig/apidef and @voxgig/struct BY
NAME, which resolved silently while they lived in the bundled scaffold
beside sdkgen's own node_modules. Out here they have to be declared, or
the components fail to type-check for the author and fail to resolve for
anyone who installs this package without sdkgen's peers present.
Peers rather than dependencies: a consumer necessarily has these already,
via sdkgen, and a second copy at a different version is the one outcome
worth preventing.
VERIFIED AS REAL MODULE IMPORTS, not grepped. A generator's components
are mostly strings containing other languages' source, so a text search
cannot tell an import from a `require` line the component EMITS — that
is how the seneca-provider migration nearly declared @seneca/maintain a
peer. Each name here was traced to a top-level import statement:
@voxgig/struct to utility_{dart,haskell,lean}.ts and TestEntity_dart.ts.
THE SDKGEN FLOOR IS THE OLDEST PUBLISHED VERSION THIS SUITE IS RUN
AGAINST, which is 4.9.0. Not the oldest that might work: a floor nobody
tests is the shape of haskell's old >=3.5.0, which accepted versions
where a target's components would install and then die at generation on
a missing export. 4.9.0 is also the first release carrying the test kit
this suite runs on.
